title: California's 5th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: California's 5th Congressional District covers a large swath of the Sierra Nevada foothills and Central Valley, including all of Amador, Calaveras, Mariposa, Mono, and Tuolumne counties, plus parts of Alpine, El Dorado, Fresno, Inyo, Madera, San Joaquin, and Stanislaus counties. Incumbent Republican Tom McClintock, first elected in 2008, is seeking re-election after advanced from the June 2 top-two primary alongside Democrat Michael Masuda, an engineer and former U.S. State Department foreign affairs officer. The district was redrawn under California Proposition 50 (2025), which altered many congressional boundaries. McClintock enters the general election as a heavy favorite, with the Cook Political Report rating the race as 'Solid Republican.' The race presents voters with a clear contrast between McClintock's long record of fiscal conservatism and deregulation and Masuda's platform emphasizing problem-solving, affordability, and wildfire preparedness.
polling_note: No independent opinion polls were found for the California's 5th Congressional District general election as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican' based on district fundamentals.

candidates.name: Tom McClintock
candidates.summary: Tom McClintock is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2008. A conservative fiscal hawk, he serves on the House Judiciary, Natural Resources, and Budget Committees. McClintock previously served in the California State Assembly (1982-1992, 1996-2000) and California State Senate (2000-2008), and ran for Governor of California in the 2003 recall election.

career_history.title: United States Representative
career_history.description: Representing California's 4th district (2009-2023) and 5th district (2023-present). Serves on House Judiciary, Natural Resources, and Budget Committees.

candidates.name: Michael Masuda
candidates.summary: Michael Masuda is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in California's 5th District, running as an engineer and former diplomat. He worked as an electrical engineer at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory for seven years before serving as a Foreign Affairs Officer at the U.S. State Department through an AAAS fellowship. Masuda grew up in Amador County and holds a degree in electrical engineering from Cal Poly San Luis Obispo. He was endorsed by the California Democratic Party and advanced from the top-two primary on June 2, 2026.
